newsitem.title: POLAND: NO POLES YET CHANGE NFI UNITS TO SHARES.
newsitem.headline: NO POLES YET CHANGE NFI UNITS TO SHARES.

text.p: None of the 26 million Poles who bought a participation unit in their country's National Investment Fund (NFI) mass privatisation scheme exchanged the unit for fund shares on Monday, the first day possible.

An employee of the National Securities Depository (KDPW) who requested anonimity told Reuters that by Monday 13,490,070 of the units had been converted into book-entry form, a step necessary for bourse trade, but none converted into NFI shares.
The units will be listed until the end of 1998.
Under the government's NFI programme, shares in more than 500 mid-sized companies are allocated to 15 NFIs run by foreign and domestic management firms.
From Monday Poles have the opportunity to exchange the unit for 15 shares, one in each fund, which are expected to start trade on the Warsaw bourse as early as mid-June.
